sanda.title: Wushu Sanda Rules and Judging
sanda.intro: Sanda is the full-contact competition format of wushu. This section gives judges a quick reference for bout structure, scoring areas, prohibited areas, scoring standards, and penalties from the 2024 rules.

rounds.title: Bout Format
rounds.description: A bout has up to three rounds. The competitor who wins two rounds wins the bout.

rest.title: Rest Period
rest.description: There is a one-minute rest period between rounds.

platform.title: Leitai
platform.description: Bouts take place on an elevated 8m by 8m platform.

validAreas.title: Valid Scoring Areas
validAreas.description: The head, torso, and thighs are valid scoring areas.

prohibitedAreas.title: Prohibited Areas
prohibitedAreas.description: The back of the head, neck, and crotch are prohibited striking areas.

twoPoints.title: Two-Point Situations
twoPoints.description: Typical two-point awards include forcing the opponent off the platform or causing the opponent to fall while remaining standing.

onePoint.title: One-Point Situations
onePoint.description: Typical one-point awards include clean effective hand or leg techniques to valid scoring areas, depending on the specific scoring case.

noScore.title: No-Score Situations
noScore.description: No points are awarded when techniques are unclear, mutually ineffective, simultaneous in a non-scoring way, or land on prohibited areas.

fouls.title: Fouls and Penalties
fouls.description: Technical and personal fouls can lead to warnings, penalty points, round loss, or disqualification according to severity.
